title: Which state's salt price rose the most in ten years?
description: A table gives the January price of iodised salt in six states over ten years. The video sets the scale for a line graph, compares Gujarat and Uttar Pradesh, then takes the first price away from the last price for every state, the same way as the rise in the book.
teaching_notes: One idea: the rise of a line is its last reading take away its first reading, worked out for each line before comparing. Watch for students who pick the state with the highest last price instead of the biggest rise.

source: Figure it Out (more on mean and median, question 9)
video_script.why: The child has found the rise of one line and now compares how six lines changed over ten years.
video_script.substitution: Choose a scale, compare the shapes of two lines, then take the first price away from the last price for each state and compare the rises.
video_script.anchor: the book's table of the January price of iodised salt in six states, from 2016 to 2025
video_script.payoff_line: west bengal rose the most, by about fourteen point five two rupees

final_answer.value: West Bengal, about 14.52 rupees; Gujarat varied less than Uttar Pradesh
final_answer.spoken: West Bengal rose the most, by about fourteen point five two rupees, and Gujarat varied less than Uttar Pradesh

never_show: the state with the highest last price is the biggest rise
maths_rules: January prices in rupees, 2016 and 2025: Andaman and Nicobar Islands 16 and 20.99; Assam 6 and 12.35; Gujarat 16.5 and 19.2; Mizoram 20 and 29.8; Uttar Pradesh 16.15 and 24.81; West Bengal 9.47 and 23.99
Andaman and Nicobar Islands 20.99 - 16 = 4.99; Assam 12.35 - 6 = 6.35; Gujarat 19.2 - 16.5 = 2.7
scale 0 to 30 in steps of 5, because the largest price is 29.8
Gujarat stays near 14 or 15 for most years and reaches 19.2 only in 2025; Uttar Pradesh climbs from 16.15 to 26.9, then dips to 24.81, so it varies more
video_script.design: One idea: work out each rise by subtraction, then compare. The table stays on the left; the line graph and the rise calculations build on the right.
open_questions: The salt table is garbled in the extracted book text; the first and last prices of each state are taken from the worklist, and every subtraction was recomputed.
